entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Peter Nigri, also known as Peter George Niger, was a prominent Dominican theologian, preacher, and controversialist whose intellectual life spanned the late 15th century, a period marked by profound religious shifts and the advent of the printing press. Born in Brünn (modern-day Brno, Czech Republic) in 1434, Nigri dedicated his career to Christian apologetics and polemics, particularly against Judaism. His work, disseminated across Central Europe, positioned him as a significant, albeit controversial, figure in the ongoing theological debates and socio-religious tensions between Christian and Jewish communities.

Nigri's most notable contribution was his 'Tractatus contra perfidos Judaeos' (Treatise against the Perfidious Jews), completed in 1475. This extensive work not only articulated traditional anti-Jewish arguments but also uniquely incorporated significant Hebrew scholarship, as Nigri was one of the first Christian scholars to study the Talmud and other rabbinic texts directly in their original language. He taught Hebrew at the newly founded University of Ingolstadt in 1476, a rare and pioneering endeavor for its time, aiming to equip Christian scholars with linguistic tools to convert Jews and refute their beliefs more effectively. His methodological approach, though rooted in polemic, foreshadowed aspects of later Christian Hebraism.
